edges.description: Loss of PBX1/HOX transcriptional programs impairs renal mesenchyme.
PBX1 loss reduces urogenital ridge outgrowth and gonadal/adrenal differentiation.
Disrupted PBX1/HOX transcription in the developing brain contributes to developmental delay (mechanism not resolved).
Disrupted branchial-arch/ear development produces ear malformations.
Disrupted Hedgehog/PBX cardiac morphogenesis produces the heart defect.
Reduced nephron endowment produces renal hypoplasia.
Impaired gonadal differentiation underlies the DSD/sex-reversal phenotype.
Reduced urogenital ridge outgrowth and gonadal differentiation underlie failed testicular descent.
Reproduces the renal hypoplasia/agenesis and nephron-deficit mechanism.
edges.limitations: The renal phenotype is characterized in homozygous nulls, which are embryonic-lethal, whereas the human disease is heterozygous haploinsufficiency; the heterozygous mouse renal phenotype was not established in the source.

edges.description: Models a disease missense allele with reduced PBX1 protein and multi-organ anomalies.
edges.limitations: The full malformation spectrum is seen in homozygotes; heterozygotes show anomalies in a proportion of embryos, matching the human dominant mode.

nodes.description: Recurrent CNV deleting PBX1; 276-kb minimal common region overlaps only PBX1.

evidence.reference_title: Paternal mosaicism for a novel PBX1 mutation associated with recurrent perinatal death: Phenotypic expansion of the PBX1-related syndrome.
evidence.snippet: the second affected sibling was stillborn at 35 weeks, presenting with similar severe bilateral diaphragmatic eventration, microsplenia, and complete sex reversal (46, XY female).

evidence.reference_title: Functional characterization of a novel PBX1 de novo missense variant identified in a patient with syndromic congenital heart disease.
evidence.snippet: we identified a de novo missense variant, PBX1:c.551G>C p.R184P, in a patient with tetralogy of Fallot with absent pulmonary valve and extra-cardiac phenotypes.

evidence.reference_title: Comprehensive overview of the role of PBX1 in mammalian kidneys.
evidence.snippet: truncating variants were shown to cause milder phenotypes (mostly cryptorchidism and deafness).

evidence.reference_title: De novo, deleterious sequence variants that alter the transcriptional activity of the homeoprotein PBX1 are associated with intellectual disability and pleiotropic developmental defects.
evidence.snippet: All patients but one had developmental delays.

evidence.reference_title: Paternal mosaicism for a novel PBX1 mutation associated with recurrent perinatal death: Phenotypic expansion of the PBX1-related syndrome.
evidence.snippet: severe bilateral diaphragmatic eventration, microsplenia, and complete sex reversal

evidence.reference_title: De novo, deleterious sequence variants that alter the transcriptional activity of the homeoprotein PBX1 are associated with intellectual disability and pleiotropic developmental defects.
evidence.snippet: including external ear anomalies, abnormal branchial arch derivatives, heart malformations, diaphragmatic hernia, renal hypoplasia and ambiguous genitalia.

evidence.reference_title: PBX1 haploinsufficiency leads to syndromic congenital anomalies of the kidney and urinary tract (CAKUT) in humans.
evidence.snippet: The most frequent extrarenal symptoms were developmental delay and ear malformations.

evidence.reference_title: De novo, deleterious sequence variants that alter the transcriptional activity of the homeoprotein PBX1 are associated with intellectual disability and pleiotropic developmental defects.
evidence.snippet: Clinical findings similar to those in Pbx mutant mice were observed in all patients with varying expressivity and severity, including external ear anomalies, abnormal branchial arch derivatives, heart malformations, diaphragmatic hernia, renal hypoplasia and ambiguous genitalia.

nodes.description: PBX1 is required in metanephric mesenchyme and stroma for mesenchymal-epithelial signalling; its loss reduces ureteric branching and nephron number, producing renal hypoplasia/dysplasia, mispositioning, or agenesis. Shown in the Pbx1-null mouse.

animal_models.description: Reproduces the renal hypoplasia/agenesis and nephron-deficit mechanism.
animal_models.name: Pbx1 knockout mouse (renal)

evidence.reference_title: Pbx1 regulates nephrogenesis and ureteric branching in the developing kidney.
evidence.snippet: Pbx1(-/-) kidneys contained fewer nephrons and were characterized by expanded regions of mesenchymal condensates in the nephrogenic zone.

evidence.reference_title: Pbx1 regulates nephrogenesis and ureteric branching in the developing kidney.
evidence.snippet: these data establish a role for Pbx1 in mesenchymal-epithelial signaling and demonstrate that Pbx1 is an essential regulator of mesenchymal function during renal morphogenesis.

nodes.description: PBX1 is widely expressed in urogenital mesenchyme; its loss reduces urogenital ridge outgrowth and impairs gonadal and adrenal differentiation, corresponding to the human differences of sex development and cryptorchidism. Shown in the Pbx1-null mouse; the human correspondence is inferred.

evidence.reference_title: Pbx1 is essential for adrenal development and urogenital differentiation.
evidence.snippet: The complete lack of adrenal glands and formation of gonads displaying rudimentary sexual differentiation correlated with decreased cellular proliferation in Pbx1(-/-) genital ridges.

nodes.description: Heterozygous PBX1 deletion, truncation, or deleterious missense reduces functional nuclear PBX1, a TALE homeodomain transcription factor that acts in multimeric complexes with HOX and other TALE proteins to regulate developmental transcription. Missense variants reduce protein, impair nuclear localization, or perturb PBX-dependent transactivation.

animal_models.description: Models a disease missense allele with reduced PBX1 protein and multi-organ anomalies.
animal_models.name: Pbx1 p.R184P knock-in mouse

biological_processes: regulation of transcription by RNA polymerase II

evidence.reference_title: De novo, deleterious sequence variants that alter the transcriptional activity of the homeoprotein PBX1 are associated with intellectual disability and pleiotropic developmental defects.
evidence.snippet: PBX1 encodes a three amino acid loop extension (TALE) homeodomain transcription factor that forms multimeric complexes with TALE and HOX proteins to regulate target gene transcription during development.

evidence.reference_title: De novo, deleterious sequence variants that alter the transcriptional activity of the homeoprotein PBX1 are associated with intellectual disability and pleiotropic developmental defects.
evidence.snippet: Functional studies on five PBX1 sequence variants revealed perturbation of intrinsic, PBX-dependent transactivation ability and altered nuclear translocation

evidence.reference_title: De novo, deleterious sequence variants that alter the transcriptional activity of the homeoprotein PBX1 are associated with intellectual disability and pleiotropic developmental defects.
evidence.snippet: We present eight patients with de novo, deleterious sequence variants in the PBX1 gene.

evidence.reference_title: PBX1 haploinsufficiency leads to syndromic congenital anomalies of the kidney and urinary tract (CAKUT) in humans.
evidence.snippet: We defined a 276-kb minimal common region (MCR) that only overlaps with the PBX1 gene. All eight patients presented with syndromic CAKUT.

nodes.description: Constitutive Pbx1 knockout; embryos show small, mispositioned kidneys with unilateral agenesis in severe cases and reduced ureteric branching.
Knock-in of the human p.R184P missense variant; heterozygotes show developmental anomalies, supporting a dominant mechanism.
Often bilateral; the most common CAKUT finding.

evidence.reference_title: PBX1 haploinsufficiency leads to syndromic congenital anomalies of the kidney and urinary tract (CAKUT) in humans.
evidence.snippet: All eight patients presented with syndromic CAKUT. CAKUT were mostly bilateral renal hypoplasia (75%).

nodes.description: De novo missense adjacent to the homeodomain; reduces PBX1 protein; tetralogy of Fallot and multi-organ anomalies (modelled in mouse).
Paternal-mosaic missense; recurrent perinatal death with 46,XY sex reversal and diaphragmatic eventration.
